body: Wednesday, August 26 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: Fed remains in a tightening-biased posture. Minutes released last week showed September rate hike still on the table. PCE inflation data released today came in sticky, reinforcing the "higher for longer" regime. GDP growth outlook is brightening even as inflation remains elevated — a stagflation-lite mix that constrains the Fed. The 10Y yield at 4.67% is climbing (+5 bps vs 4W), while the 2Y at 4.17% (prior close) has slipped 9 bps, leaving a +47 bps curve — positively sloped but still flat by historical standards. Trump continues to publicly call for lower rates, creating political friction with new Fed Chair Warsh ahead of his Friday speech.

New / Most Important: Today's PCE print stayed sticky, confirming the Fed's hawkish lean is data-justified. Fed minutes from last week explicitly kept a September hike alive — this is the key new development. The dollar devaluation trade has restarted on Wall Street per multiple reports, with DXY holding near 99 (we lack a live DXY snapshot but headlines confirm weakness). This is structurally important: equities rallying (S&P at 7668, ↑4.8%) alongside a weakening dollar and surging gold (4646, ↑15.2%) suggests capital is pricing in fiscal dominance — markets believe the US will ultimately inflate its way through debt burdens regardless of what the Fed does. The bond market is "resetting expectations" per multiple outlets, and the VIX at 15.68 (↓24.1%) screams complacency against this backdrop.

Playbook ✓: Mega-cap tech dominance continues — Nasdaq ↑7.3% vs Russell ↑3.3%, confirming narrow market leadership. Nvidia earnings tonight are the consensus event risk.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The simultaneous dollar weakness, equity strength, and gold surge is NOT the standard playbook. Normally a weakening dollar with rising yields implies capital flight or fiscal credibility erosion — yet equities are ripping higher. This is the capital-flow signature of a regime where foreign investors are diversifying out of US Treasuries but rotating INTO US equities (particularly mega-cap tech as a dollar-hedge proxy). Gold surging to three-month highs as the dollar weakens confirms this isn't a healthy risk-on move — it's a bifurcated market where real assets and nominal risk assets are both being bid as stores of value against fiat debasement expectations. Watch US Treasury buyback programs closely — headlines suggest these may be redirecting capital toward Asia, further weakening the dollar recycling mechanism that has underpinned US fixed income for decades.

Macro Stance: The ECB is setting up for a September rate hike, with Schnabel explicitly stating the ECB must raise rates further to contain inflation. The stance is hawkish but measured — "no appetite to signal more" beyond September suggests a one-and-done posture.

New / Most Important: The ECB September hike is now consensus per today's headlines. German economy grew slightly faster than expected, providing cover for further tightening. Morningstar flagged that Europe's low tech weighting is a structural advantage in the current environment — with the DAX defying uncertainty, European equities are outperforming on a risk-adjusted basis precisely because they lack the AI concentration risk.

Playbook ✓: Euro weakening against yen on BOJ hike bets is textbook rate-differential trading. ECB tightening supports EUR vs USD but not vs JPY.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The euro is falling despite the ECB hike signal — this breaks the standard monetary policy → currency channel. The explanation is that markets view the ECB hike as a policy error in a structurally weaker growth environment, meaning the rate increase will be short-lived. If the euro can't rally on a hike signal, the currency has a credibility problem that benefits European exporters but signals deeper macro skepticism.

Macro Stance: China remains in an accommodative posture, and the PBOC has started using the exchange rate as an easing tool. The loan prime rates were left steady for a 15th consecutive month (Reuters, [Aug 19]), the one-year at 3.0% and the five-year at 3.5% (BigGo Finance, [Aug 19]); liquidity runs through overnight reverse repos (Xinhua, [Aug 24]) and a 500 billion yuan MLF operation (BigGo Finance, [Aug 24]), and banks now use the overnight rate to price bonds as the PBOC reform widens (Bloomberg, [Aug 25]). After the yuan surged to 6.72, a 42-month high (BigGo Finance, [Aug 20]), the PBOC set a weaker fix above the Reuters estimate, signalling tolerance for depreciation to bolster growth (VT Markets, [Aug 25]), and the yuan slipped from its 3-1/2-year high (The Star, [Aug 25]). July CPI slowed to 0.5% and PPI to 3.5%, both missing expectations (BigGo Finance, [Aug 8]): there is room to ease.

PMIs & Activity: The data are the weak leg of the bull case. July's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.2 and non-manufacturing to 49.0 (FXStreet, [Jul 31]); the private factory index eased to 50.9 (Fibre2Fashion, [Aug 3]) and private services growth hit its slowest since September 2024 (Reuters, [Aug 4]). July industrial output grew 4.5% y/y and retail sales only 0.6% (Reuters, [Aug 17]), and fixed-asset investment fell 6.7% in the first seven months (Xinhua, [Aug 17]). Exports are the offset, jumping almost a quarter in July (Financial Times, [Aug 6]) on AI-driven shipments. That is why Goldman says easing hopes revive with the economy growing 4% (Bloomberg, [Aug 23]) while warning Q3 growth could fall below 4.5% (BigGo Finance, [Aug 24]). First-half profits rose 18.7% as a tech boom masked the property slump (Caixin Global, [Jul 27]).

Credit Impulse: July bank loans posted a record contraction as credit demand faltered (Reuters, [Aug 14]), yet credit growth exceeded forecasts despite the rare loan slump (Bloomberg, [Aug 14]). Reconciled: the broad financing aggregate is holding up while the loan book itself shrank, so the impulse comes from outside bank lending. Policy is working on price rather than volume: corporate loan rates fell below 3% (BigGo Finance, [Aug 14]) and the subsidized loan program was expanded to revive demand (Caixin Global, [Aug 21]), with the SME loan cap raised to 75 million yuan. Liquidity is ample; demand for it is the missing piece.

Property: July new home prices were stagnant as demand stayed weak (Reuters, [Aug 17]); the 70-city annual decline narrowed to 3.2%, the smallest in five months, while property investment slumped nearly 20% (BigGo Finance, [Aug 17]). The monthly picture is softer, with prices falling at a faster pace (Bloomberg, [Aug 17]) and first-tier prices flat, ending a four-month rebound (SCMP, [Aug 17]). Easing continues at the margin: Beijing widened use of a $1.6 trillion fund to spur spending on homes (The Business Times, [Aug 19]) and Shanghai lowered second-home down payments (SCMP, [Aug 20]). The legacy is being closed out: Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan was sentenced to life in prison (Reuters, [Aug 20]) and a court accepted the Evergrande liquidation a day later (SCMP, [Aug 21]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Fiscal policy is the lever, but it will be targeted. China pledged timely fiscal support to bolster growth (Reuters, [Aug 20]) and optimised fiscal and financial policies to lift demand (Fibre2Fashion, [Aug 25]), yet key state media commentaries signal no "bazooka" (Caixin Global, [Aug 25]) and the $119 billion policy financing tool faces a roll-out lag (Reuters, [Aug 24]). On trade, the US eyes overcapacity tariffs of 7.5% before the Xi-Trump talks (Bloomberg, [Aug 24]), China warned the US it could retaliate over Iran sanctions (Financial Times, [Aug 25]), and EU officials will travel to China as the October deadline looms (Euronews.com, [Aug 25]), with Goldman estimating EU curbs threaten 27% of Chinese exports to the bloc (Bloomberg, [Aug 24]).

Markets & Flows: Business Insider's call to start paying attention to China's economy again captures the shift in sentiment, and capital is pivoting into physical AI, with Xpeng posting a huge funding round for its robotics unit. Near term, supply weighs: China stocks hit a near one-month low (TradingView, [Aug 25]) as Alibaba sells $10 billion of stock while major figures buy (MarketWatch, [Aug 25]), and Unitree's post-listing slump sparks bubble fears (Reuters, [Aug 25]). Dollar weakness, US Treasury buybacks reportedly redirecting capital toward Asia and Indian investors pouring record funds into overseas stocks support the flow picture.

New / Most Important: The PBOC has moved from slowing the yuan's gains to signalling tolerance for depreciation. That is the easing the bull case needed: a weaker fix loosens conditions for exporters without an LPR cut, at the moment state media rule out a bazooka. The risk has moved to trade, where Beijing's warning that it could retaliate over Iran sanctions lands weeks before the Xi-Trump talks and alongside a 7.5% overcapacity tariff threat.

Playbook ✓: Dollar weakness benefiting EM and China capital flows is textbook, and a PBOC that leans against yuan strength while pledging fiscal support fits the easing script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The bull case rests on flows and policy, not activity: the PMI is 49.2, the loan book shrank and property investment is down nearly 20%. A yuan held back from its high plus weak domestic demand means China exports price pressure rather than demand, which hits European exporters already facing the October deadline, while iron ore trades stimulus hopes, rising on fresh stimulus signals (TradingView, [Aug 24]) after weakening despite them (TradingView, [Aug 23]). If fiscal support stays targeted, the AUD and EM commodity exporters carry the downside, and WTI at 82.82 remains a terms-of-trade tax on China.

Macro Stance: The BOJ is now firmly on course to hike in September, with the timeline accelerated by yen weakness. Goldman Sachs pulled forward its hike call and now sees a terminal rate of 1.75%. This is a structural regime change for global capital flows.

New / Most Important: This is the most important macro story globally right now. The BOJ hiking to 1.25% in September — with Goldman targeting 1.75% terminal — fundamentally reprices the yen carry trade that has funded risk assets worldwide for over a decade. Former BOJ board members are publicly stating that risks of NOT hiking outweigh the risks of hiking, which is extraordinary hawkish signaling from Japan's traditionally dovish establishment. Every major currency is weakening against the yen (EUR, GBP, USD). The speed of this repricing matters enormously: if BOJ tightening accelerates carry trade unwinds, the liquidity drain hits risk assets globally — particularly US tech and EM, which have been the primary beneficiaries of yen-funded leverage. The August 2024 carry unwind was a preview; this time the BOJ is signaling with more conviction and the market is better positioned but the structural flow reversal is larger. Watch JPY crosses as the leading indicator for global risk appetite into September.

Playbook ✓: Yen strengthening against all majors is textbook rate-hike anticipation.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The divergence is that equities globally are NOT yet pricing the carry unwind — S&P ↑4.8%, Nasdaq ↑7.3%, VIX at complacent 15.68. This disconnect between JPY rate expectations and equity vol is the single biggest fragility in markets today.

Macro Stance: The RBA is back on alert after July inflation ran hotter than expected. Markets have repriced rate hike risk sharply — "flipped the script" per AFR. The August meeting revealed a divided board that debated hiking, confirming the hawkish bias.

New / Most Important: Australia's inflation surprise is the key development. This is structurally significant because Australia is now the last major DM economy where the inflation problem is arguably worsening rather than plateauing. The RBA simultaneously launched a new demand-driven liquidity regime ("Road to Ample"), which is an operational shift in how it manages reserves — a technical change but one that signals the RBA is modernizing its plumbing while maintaining hawkish policy. A fourth rate hike would be genuinely painful for Australian households already stretched by mortgage resets. The housing-centric economy makes Australia the most rate-sensitive DM market, yet inflation is forcing the RBA's hand.

Playbook ✓: Hot inflation → hawkish repricing is textbook.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The divergence is China — its July official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.2 and property investment slumped nearly 20%, so Australia gets no lift from Chinese demand, yet the RBA can't ease. This creates an unusual dynamic where external demand softens but domestic demand must be crushed via rates. AUD is caught between soft Chinese demand, which saw it soften as Beijing leaned against yuan gains, and the global dollar weakness narrative.

Macro Stance: The question has been put in print: Tysol.pl asks whether rates go up, calling it an important signal for Poland [Aug 26], days after reporting which RPP members wanted a hike [Aug 22]. The activity backdrop supports the hawks on balance. CEO Magazyn sums up the July batch as an economy still growing, industry strong, construction a surprise decline [Aug 26]; PAP asks whether large firms investing again marks a new growth phase [Aug 26]. The softer side is the consumer, with July retail sales up 3.9% y/y in constant prices (Inwestycje.pl, [Aug 24]) but below forecasts (Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK, [Aug 24]), and unemployment at 5.8% (Forsal.pl, [Aug 25]) with wages up 6.8% (Do Rzeczy, [Aug 20]). Fuel relief arrives tonight, with cheaper prices from just after midnight (Rzeczpospolita, [Aug 26]), while Portal Spożywczy sees prices rising ever more slowly but a turning point ahead [Aug 25].

Markets: The WIG20 finally bounced off 4000 points (Parkiet, [Aug 26]), up 0.7% with PGE more than 5% higher (Bankier.pl, [Aug 26]) as cheaper oil lifted the WIG and brought PGE and KGHM back to gains (XTB.com, [Aug 26]), and PKO BP printed a new all-time high (DNA Rynków, [Aug 26]). Żabka was the centre of attention (Parkiet, [Aug 26]) after Couche-Tard launched a tender offer for all its shares (Reuters, [Aug 26]); Strefa Biznesu argues the proceeds may go to tax havens and that Dino gains from the shake-up [Aug 26]. The card reflects Tuesday's close: KGHM 366.0 (+9.4% 1W, +25.1% 4W) and Dino 36.18 (+11.4% 1W, +14.3% 4W) are the leaders, PKO 113.52 (+3.3% 1W), Pekao 257.1 (+1.3% 1W, +8.2% 4W) and PGE 10.54 (+2.4% 1W, +6.5% 4W) firm, EPOL 44.69 (+2.4% 1W, +8.4% 4W), while CD Projekt 242.9 (-6.0% 1W) carries the Witcher 4 damage and LPP 20,700 (-1.5% 1W) and Allegro 44.87 (-0.5% 1W) drift. The zloty is pushing the euro to a key level while the dollar froze ahead of the US reading (Bankier.pl, [Aug 26]); the card has USD/PLN 3.684 (-1.3% 1W, -3.0% 4W) and EUR/PLN 4.3005 (-0.4% 1W, -0.6% 4W), though Comparic.pl flagged an intraday reversal today [Aug 26]. POLGBs: billions are flowing into bond funds but Analizy.pl asks where the returns are [Aug 26], Pimco says bonds are attractive because the term premium will stay elevated (pb.pl, [Aug 24]).

Fiscal & Politics: The veto fight turned personal. After the finance ministry presented its bill for the president's vetoes, the Palace called it an inept manipulation (Interia, Fakt, [Aug 26]) and Nawrocki's spokesman answered the salty invoice (TVN24, [Aug 26]); Rzeczpospolita had put the cost at billions of zloty [Aug 25]. The government decided the lump-sum taxation rules, including the fate of the 15% rate (Gazeta Prawna, [Aug 26]). The 4.8 billion zł support for energy-intensive firms comes with conditions on renewables and decarbonisation investment (ESG Trends, [Aug 26]), and KGHM, Orlen and Grupa Azoty are lobbying for changes to the energy ministry's tariff draft, which Interia says could exclude the largest firms [Aug 26]. A rare positive from the public sector: finance ministry data show local governments running surpluses instead of deficits (Serwis Samorządowy PAP, [Aug 26]). Fitch's A- with negative outlook (PAP, [Aug 22]) remains the frame.

Corporate & Sectors: Orlen started production from three new Norwegian fields a year ahead of plan (StockWatch.pl, [Aug 26]), adding over 4 billion cubic metres of gas (WNP.PL, [Aug 26]); an analyst raised valuations of Orlen and Unimot on exceptional macro conditions (pb.pl, [Aug 26]). KGHM and its partner reported copper resources up 61% (Parkiet, [Aug 26]), the company plans polyhalite mining at Puck Bay (PCH24.pl, [Aug 26]) and Energetyka24 confirms it as the world's largest silver producer [Aug 26], though wnp.pl warns record copper prices could become a problem for it [Aug 26]. CD Projekt announced a Witcher 3 remaster and showed the Songs of the Past trailer (StockWatch.pl, [Aug 26]); DM BOŚ expects the expansion in the first quarter of 2027 (BIZNES24, [Aug 26]), Parkiet asks whether the sell-off is a buying opportunity [Aug 26], pb.pl's analyst says hold [Aug 26] and Bankier.pl reports short positions rising [Aug 26]; half-year results are due next week (CD PROJEKT RED IR, [Aug 26]). PKO BP is contesting the 47.5 million zł KNF fine and asked for the case to be reconsidered (pb.pl, [Aug 26]). Dino keeps rising despite weaker results as analysts revisit the stock (Wiadomości Handlowe, [Aug 26]) and opens stores at scale while Biedronka fights on price (DlaHandlu.pl, [Aug 26]); LPP has 150 stores in Hungary (Retailnet.pl, [Aug 26]); Allegro was cheaper in nearly 77% of almost 20 thousand price comparisons (aboutmarketing.pl, [Aug 26]).

Geopolitics & Security: Forsal.pl reports Russian exercises near the NATO border rehearsing saboteurs first and an armed attack second [Aug 26]; NATO is weighing the cost of shooting back at escalating drone incursions (The Kyiv Independent, [Aug 24]) and is taking measures against Moscow's direct actions from drones to sabotage (Il Foglio, [Aug 26]). Poland detained a Ukrainian over an alleged Russian-backed assassination plot (TVP World, [Aug 20]).

New / Most Important: Orlen's Norwegian gas and the Żabka tender matter more than the index bounce. Upstream volume a year early is a direct hedge on the energy CIT the company is about to pay, and a full takeover of Żabka is a foreign strategic buyer validating Polish consumer assets at the moment a British fund is short the market. The veto dispute, now a public shouting match, is the risk that overlays both.  |  Playbook ✓: Hold; KGHM and Dino as earnings-backed longs, add Orlen on upstream delivery, banks at highs on mortgage flow, zloty strength ridden on the dollar leg, duration light until the budget.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Record copper is being read as a problem for KGHM by wnp.pl while the stock prints +25% in four weeks; if cost inflation and tariff exclusion bite, the leader of this rally is also its most crowded trade.

Macro Stance: Indian investors deployed record funds into overseas stocks and debt in June, confirming India as a new structural source of global portfolio flows. Nepal is trending on X — context appears non-financial but bears monitoring for geopolitical developments.

New / Most Important: India's record overseas investment flows are structurally important — this is a new marginal buyer entering global markets at scale, diversifying away from domestic concentration.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: South Korea's rookie investors losing money on AI stocks is a classic late-cycle retail capitulation signal for the AI trade in Asia.

Narrative: Mega-cap tech dominance keeps widening, with the Nasdaq ↑7.3% vs the Russell ↑3.3% over four weeks; Microsoft earned 31% more yet its stock is worth less, so the bar for big tech keeps rising into Nvidia's report tonight.

Reported: Intuit tumbled despite an earnings beat as weak 2027 guidance weighed on the shares (TradingView, [Aug 25]). Keysight's shares rose after record third-quarter results (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 19]). Ubiquiti beat by $0.25 and topped revenue estimates (Investing.com, [Aug 21]).

EPS Upside Watch: Salesforce — rising Agentforce adoption is expected to aid sales in its Q2 report (TradingView, [Aug 25]), an AI revenue line that can lift the guide. Dell — earnings are expected to grow (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 25]), with analysts saying the print could propel a stock up 235% this year even higher (MarketWatch, [Aug 24]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Software is crushing chips by a record margin (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 25]) even as Microsoft, earning 31% more, is worth less: the market pays for AI revenue that shows up in the guide, not for AI capex. Intuit's tumble on a weak 2027 guide shows the software rally offers no slack either.
Narrative: Meta is the story: its $18 billion mid-trial settlement in the teen addiction case removes a major overhang and the stock rose, while the sector keeps riding the Nasdaq's leadership.

Reported: Zoom's revenue rose on enterprise growth (WSJ, [Aug 25]), but it gave a lukewarm outlook despite an expanded product line (Bloomberg.com, [Aug 25]). Kuaishou's earnings dropped by a third, hit by AI and creator costs (Bloomberg.com, [Aug 19]). NetEase fell as a Q2 earnings miss overshadowed stronger revenue (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 20]).
EPS Upside Watch: JOYY — Q2 revenue rose 16% as AI drove growth across three core businesses, and it raised its full-year profit guidance (BigGo Finance, [Aug 25]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: AI is a cost line before it is a revenue line: Kuaishou and NetEase missed, and Alibaba slid as Q2 profit missed estimates despite strong AI cloud growth (Investing.com Nigeria, [Aug 20]). Meta's $18B settlement prices the other hidden cost, youth-safety liability, and gives every social platform a number to model.

Narrative: JPMorgan is approaching a $1 trillion market cap, a 10Y at 4.67% and a +47 bps curve support modest NIM expansion, and US banking profits improved as lending expanded (Bloomberg.com, [Aug 25]).

Reported: BMO and Scotiabank beat profit estimates and brushed aside tariff worries (Reuters, [Aug 25]) as their capital-markets units surged (Bloomberg.com, [Aug 25]), and the TSX hit a record high as Scotiabank jumped on its report (Reuters, [Aug 25]). Bendigo Bank's H2 profit rose, but its shares fell (Investing.com, [Aug 23]).

EPS Upside Watch: BMO — plans to buy back shares after a strong quarter (WSJ, [Aug 25]), a direct per-share lift. US banks — an Anthropic IPO that avoids SpaceX's slump is key for their earnings (Bloomberg.com, [Aug 25]), with underwriting fees the lever.

⚡ Breaking Convention: JPMorgan easing lending standards for SpaceX-linked wealth is a credit-cycle signal: banks relaxing underwriting for 'new economy' borrowers typically happens late in cycles, and tying it explicitly to AI wealth concentration rather than broad credit expansion makes it a novel risk.

Narrative: WTI at 82.82 (↓1.9% vs 4W) is weakening despite Hormuz risk and Bessent's 'D-Day' Iran sanctions plan, as supply-shock narratives fade and demand outside China, with the US flash composite PMI at 56 in August, sets the price.

Reported: Woodside posted a 7% first-half profit rise while scrapping its clean energy target (Reuters, [Aug 24]). Sinopec's H1 profit rose 19.3% as its chemicals segment returned to profit after 16 quarters (BigGo Finance, [Aug 23]). Ithaca Energy raised its 2026 dividend guidance after record North Sea production (Yahoo Finance UK, [Aug 19]).
EPS Upside Watch: Midstream — strong 2Q26 earnings are boosting the full-year outlook (ETF Trends, [Aug 25]), fee-based volumes rather than the oil price.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Oil falling while Iran sanctions escalate means demand, not supply, is driving the complex: August flash PMIs show the US and euro zone accelerating while China's July factory PMI sat at 49.2, so the bid is not Chinese. The political cap is rising too, as six countries want EU talks in September on taxing oil companies' windfall profits (Reuters, [Aug 24]).

Narrative: Aerospace and defence private-equity exit value has already beaten last year's total, and Hyundai's commitment to build more cars in the US confirms the reshoring capex cycle, while AI construction is feeding machinery guidance.

Reported: Deere rallied 7% after quarterly profit climbed and it raised its full-year forecast (TIKR.com, [Aug 21]), with data-centre construction bolstering its sales guidance (Manufacturing Dive, [Aug 21]). Heico beat estimates on aerospace and defence demand (Seeking Alpha, [Aug 25]). Ashtead Technology shares sank after a 2026 revenue and profit warning (Yahoo Finance UK, [Aug 20]).

EPS Upside Watch: Delta — CEO Ed Bastian says AI could boost profits by 50% as the airline tests AI-set fares on 3% of tickets (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 24]). Southwest — S&P upgraded its outlook on earnings growth (Investing.com, [Aug 25]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: XPeng's robotics business raised $900 mln in its first funding round (Global Times, [Aug 25]). Chinese automation capital at that scale will eventually pressure Western industrial-automation margins, a risk the reshoring story leaves out.

Narrative: Abercrombie & Fitch soaring is the brand-resurrection trade continuing, and consumer spending is holding up despite higher rates as the GDP growth outlook brightens: execution is beating the macro headwinds.

Reported: Dick's Sporting Goods fell 30% as it missed expectations and cited a 'challenging' footwear market (CNBC, [Aug 25]), and it cut guidance (WSJ, [Aug 25]). Ross Stores surged 9% after beating and lifting guidance (TIKR.com, [Aug 21]). Advance Auto Parts plunged 21% as a revenue miss overshadowed its earnings beat (24/7 Wall St., [Aug 20]).

EPS Upside Watch: Lowe's — the CEO says its $80M tariff refund could be just a fraction of the total payout (The Business Journals, [Aug 24]). Expedia — jumped after Evercore ISI raised its target to $430 (TIKR.com, [Aug 25]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: 41% of workers delaying medical care and 1-in-4 raiding retirement savings, per Suze Orman, is a stark warning beneath the topline spending data. The Foot Locker owner plunged after warning that nervous consumers are cutting spending (Financial Times, [Aug 25]): the gap between brand winners like Abercrombie and stress at the median is widening.
Narrative: Defensive staples underperform in a risk-on tape, and the mass-market shopper is fraying: Walmart's shares slumped on its weakest sales growth in over six years (WSJ, [Aug 20]).

Reported: Walmart tumbled 9% after its outlook disappointed (CNBC, [Aug 20]), even though it raised full-year guidance as US comparable sales growth slowed to just 2.6% (The Motley Fool, [Aug 20]). Target boosted its 2026 outlook after a Q2 sales and earnings beat (Yahoo Finance UK, [Aug 19]). Estée Lauder surged on an earnings beat and raised margin guidance (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 19]).
EPS Upside Watch: BJ's Wholesale — beat and raised its full-year EPS guidance (Quartz, [Aug 21]). Smucker — named among food stocks that can defy GLP-1 fears (Barron's, [Aug 19]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Tariff refunds, not shoppers, are doing the lifting: Target's profit nearly doubled but the biggest contributor wasn't more shopping (Inc.com, [Aug 19]), and Walmart's operating income jumped 17.4% on tariff refunds (BigGo Finance, [Aug 20]). A one-off refund cannot hide a volume problem, which is why Walmart fell on a raise.

Narrative: Workers delaying medical care signal demand destruction at the point of service, a negative for utilization plays, and Spyre Therapeutics' plunge keeps biotech a binary stock-picker's market.

Reported: Telix's first-half profit surged 146% on strong precision-medicine demand (TIKR.com, [Aug 23]). Hengrui saw profit growth squeezed by China's bulk-buying programs (Reuters, [Aug 19]). Alvotech missed Q2 estimates as revenue stalled (Investing.com, [Aug 20]).
EPS Upside Watch: Pharmaron — raised its full-year revenue guidance, and Goldman Sachs and Daiwa lifted their target prices (BigGo Finance, [Aug 24]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: The bearish utilization story misses the supply chain: Pharmaron's raised guide and Telix's profit surge show outsourced R&D and precision medicine growing while point-of-service demand softens. Pricing is the real constraint, as Ardelyx cut guidance on payer hurdles (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 22]).
Narrative: Copper at 6.70 (↑6.9% vs 4W) rides the AI data-centre and grid-capex bid, gold at 4646 (↑15.2%) pulls gold miners higher, and miners are rising even on down days.

Reported: SQM rose after an earnings beat and a higher lithium outlook (Reuters, [Aug 19]). Evolution Mining posted record EBITDA and dividend (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 19]). Lundin Mining cut its copper outlook as Chile storms struck again (Mining.com, [Aug 19]), less supply of the AI data-centre and grid metal.
EPS Upside Watch: Novonesis — beat expectations and raised its guidance (The Copenhagen Post, [Aug 20]). Kaiser Aluminum — its H2 2026 update justifies a price target raise (Seeking Alpha, [Aug 20]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Gold (↑15.2%) is outpacing copper (↑6.9%): materials are bid, but the mix favours precious metals and AI/grid-exposed copper over China-cyclical industrials, with China's official factory PMI at 49.2 in July. Storm-hit copper supply, as copper miners cut 2026 guidance (Industrial Info, [Aug 21]), tightens the AI and grid metal without any help from Chinese demand.
Narrative: Rising 10Y yields (4.67%, +5 bps vs 4W) are a direct headwind, and rate-sensitive real estate stays under pressure with both the Fed and ECB tilting toward hikes.
